https://www.dw.com/en/donald-trump-to-de.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IrdL Trump said Americans must accept having to 'pay a tiny little bit more for your gasoline' Image: Yuki Iwamura/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement President Donald Trump said Friday that he would "soon" declare the Strait of Hormuz a US territory. "After we finish defeating Iran , which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States," Trump said at a rally at a police academy in Garden City, New York state. "It's true," he added. It was not clear whether his remarks were serious or whether they signal a new policy shift for Washington in its war against Tehran , which is more than five months old. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi dismissed Trump's remarks, saying the country would "not be intimidated" and that the strategic waterway would remain under its control and authority. What is the situation in the Strait of Hormuz? The US and Israel launched the war against Iran on February 28. At the time, senior White House officials, including Trump, said the aim was to end Iran's nuclear program and spark a popular uprising to force regime change in the Islamic Republic, among other goals. Iran's response has been to target US allies across the Middle East with drone and missile strikes, as well as to impose a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments passed before the war. The US responded to Iran's closure of the strait with its own naval blockade of Iranian ships and ports. The two countries have been locked in a stalemate over the vital waterway for months, causing energy prices to soar. Rising oil and gas costs and the economic fallout from the war are likely to be leading issues in the midterm elections in November. What if Iran and Oman split control of the Strait of Hormuz? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What else did Trump say during the rally in Garden City? During the rally, the US president also urged Americans to accept that they would have to "pay a tiny little bit more" for their gasoline as a worthy price for preventing "a very evil country" from getting a nuclear weapon. "What we're doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves ... and we're really doing a ​great job," Trump told the crowd, adding that "no ships get through (the US blockade of Hormuz) unless we want them to." On Friday, Trump also dismissed concerns over the living conditions aboard a US aircraft carrier that was deployed to the Middle East amid the war with Iran. Relatives of service members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln told US military media outlets that personnel are struggling with difficult living conditions and deteriorating mental health . There have also been reports of suicide attempts. Trump denied that the deployment of the aircraft carrier , which has been at sea for nine months, had lasted too long, instead insisting that the aircraft carrier's deployment was "not nearly enough." He also confirmed that the ship would be replaced by another "very similar" vessel. https://www.dw.com/en/canada-ukraine-ple.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MM18 Zelenskyy and Carney signed a '100-year parntership' between Ukraine and Canada in Calgary Image: Ahmed Zakot/REUTERS Advertisement Canada and Ukraine on Thursday signed a declaration vowing to keep a 100-year partnership between the two countries. It comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visits the country for talks with Prime Minister Mark Carney and other Canadian officials. Zelenskyy and Carney said that Canada had pledged to help shore up Ukraine's air defense. "Earlier today, Canada and Ukraine finalized an agreement to deliver critical air defense interceptors (through) the United States Jumpstart mechanism," Carney said. He said that the package would amount to some 350 million Canadian dollars ($260 million, €218 million). The prime minister said that Canada had provided the equivalent of 26 billion Canadian dollars ($19 billion, €16 billion) in support for Ukraine. "We've provided support for the energy systems and beyond. We'll provide more support," he said. Zelenskyy expressed his graitude for what he described as a "very important" air defense package. "I'm so thankful," Zelenskyy said. "This is very important package of air defense and this is crucial." Speaking ahead of his meeting with Zelenskyy, Carney also emphasized Ukrainians' historical role in contributing to European settlement in the prairies of Canada's western provinces. "Ukrainians help build ​this province, ⁠this country. Canada will help rebuild Ukraine when peace comes," he said, referring to Alberta, of which Calgary is the largest city. Canada is home to over a million people of Ukrainian descent. Zelenskyy and his wife Olena arrived in Canada late on Wednesday Image: Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Zelenskyy visits Canada after Norway Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in Calgary late on Wednesday for "important meetings ​and agreements" with Canadian officials. His visit comes on the heels of his attendance at King Harald V's funeral in Norway, where his plane had been delayed by a drone incursion . The Ukrainian leader is in the middle of a flurry of trips and meetings to shore up his country's defenses for the cold winter months . "The main focus will be on supporting Ukraine in protecting our skies and preparing for the winter," Zelenskyy said in a social media post before leaving. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement that the visit "will focus on shared priorities between Canada and Ukraine, including deepening defense, economic, and energy cooperation." Carney's statement added Canada "remains steadfast in our commitment to support Ukraine's defense, recovery, and reconstruction." Zelenskyy had also signaled a desire to meet with US President Donald Trump on the matter before the end of September. Since Russia's invasion in 2022, Moscow has consistently increased attacks on fuel and heating infrastructure in Ukraine in the autumn and winter. What is happening on the battlefield? Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery in the Yamalo-Nenets region overnight, as well as a seaport in Dagestan, Zelenskyy said. He added that other unnamed sited critical to Russia's war industry had also been hit. Alexander Gusev, governor of Russia's Voronezh region, said that one woman in the town of Borisoglebsk had been killed by falling drone debris overnight and that at least 19 drones had been destroyed while flying over the region. The Russian Defense Ministry said a total of 448 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight. In Ukraine, Russian attacks hit buildings owned by a major food producer in Dnipro, killing at least two according to local officials. Two Azerbaijani crew members were killed in a drone attack on a cargo ship in the Ukrainian region of Odesa, Ukraine's infrastructure ministry said. Azerbaijan's foreign ministry also confirmed the information, adding that two further members of the crew were taken to hospital in Chornomorsk, Ukraine. While Baku did not mention who was responsible for the attack, Ukraine blamed Russia for the drone strike. Torrential rain and flooding slam Tunis, forcing schools to close Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 18/09/2026 - 16:26 GMT+2 Torrential rain and severe thunderstorms struck Tunis on 17 September, flooding roads, disrupting traffic, and forcing schools and universities to suspend afternoon classes from 3 p.m. local time. … More The Tunis Governorate announced suspension of afternoon classes across all public and private educational, training, and university institutions, citing warnings from the National Institute of Meteorology and advice from the regional disaster-prevention committee. Between 30 and 50 millimetres of rain were forecast across Greater Tunis in a short period, overwhelming drainage systems in several neighbourhoods. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Water quickly covered roads and pavements, forcing residents to wade through flooded streets. Cars and buses struggled to pass, with some vehicles left stranded and one trapped beneath a tunnel. In the historic medina , residents took refuge in shops and under awnings as torrents of water swept through the narrow streets. The storm also caused power and internet cuts and sent water into some homes. Footage shared on social media appeared to show power lines catching fire amid the heavy downpour. The rainfall came after a summer of prolonged heatwaves and follows a year of repeated flooding. In January , at least five people died when Tunisia recorded its heaviest rainfall in more than seven decades. The latest storms have once again highlighted the pressure that extreme rainfall can place on Tunis’ infrastructure , particularly after long periods of intense heat. Photograph: David Gray/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen A 13-year-old boy has been charged with murder after a man was stabbed to death in Mount Druitt in Sydney’s west on Friday. Photograph: David Gray/AFP/Getty Images Sydney ‘Absolutely senseless’: boy, 13, charged with murder after man stabbed to death in Sydney’s west The 36-year-old victim had withdrawn cash to give to some young people when he was allegedly stabbed, according to police Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Nick Visser Sun 11 Oct 2026 18.39 EDT Last modified on Sun 11 Oct 2026 23.15 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 13-year-old boy has been charged with murder after a man was stabbed to death in Sydney’s west on Friday. Emergency services were called to the suburb of Mount Druitt on Friday evening amid reports a man had been assaulted. Police found the man, 36, with stab wounds to his torso. Paramedics assisted the man but he died at the scene. A boy, 13, was arrested on Sunday at Mount Druitt police station and charged with murder, breach of bail and an unrelated offence of robbery. Police said Monday the boy was known to them and an investigator recognised him on CCTV footage from the incident. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email A second boy, 16, was arrested at a home in Cabramatta later Sunday evening. He was charged with being accessory after the fact to murder. “In my 30-year career of policing, I find this absolutely senseless,” Supt Darrin Batchelor said during a news briefing on Monday. Batchelor said initial investigations say the altercation seemed to stem from a “chance meeting that was totally innocent”. He said the man was on his way home from work and stopped to speak to a group of young people he knew through family and friends. The man later went to an ATM to withdraw money so the young people he knew “could head home that night”. “Another group of young people took offence to that conversation … and as a result of that we now stand here today with that 36-year-old male … now [allegedly] murdered,” Batchelor said. “Here you have an individual … on his way home from work, purely stopped to talk to friends that he knew, and this group took offence to that and allegedly stabbed him twice,” he went on. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Officials encouraged anyone with information, including CCTV or dashcam footage, to come forward, saying inquiries continued. Supt Brendan Gorman told reporters over the weekend detectives were looking into the alleged murder, saying there were about “a dozen people” in the area at the time of the stabbing. Police said Monday they know of at least two others allegedly involved in the incident, and encouraged them to turn themselves in. A knife allegedly used in the stabbing was recovered after the incident in a drain outside a unit block in Cabramatta. Both boys were refused bail to appear before a children’s court on Monday. This story was amended on 12 October 2026. An earlier version incorrectly stated the victim’s age as 30, rather than 36. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/07/meno.text: Lenzetto, one of the most widely used hormone treatments to relieve menopausal symptoms, will once again be available in Spanish pharmacies from the second half of November, its manufacturer Gedeon Richter has confirmed to Euronews."We expect the product to be available in pharmacies from the second half of November," the pharmaceutical company said in response to questions from Euronews. Gedeon Richter says it will do "everything possible" to guarantee stable production for the rest of this year and in 2027, although it acknowledges that worldwide supply constraints may prevent it from fully covering current demand.The company traces the origin of the current shortage of the medicine in Spain to a sharp rise in demand for menopause hormone treatments in Europe. In an email, the company explained that growth has been far higher than expected and that both manufacturing capacity and the supply of the device used to administer Lenzetto, the applicator, could not keep pace with the surge in demand.Gedeon Richter stresses that the situation is temporary and "is not related to any problem with the quality or safety of the medicine". The issue, according to the company, is simply that high demand has outstripped its production capacity.To increase the availability of its medicine, the laboratory says it is making full use of its current production capacity and working to expand both the number of suppliers and its manufacturing options. It is also trying to improve the supply of applicators and increase their production capacity, among other measures.These plans include a new plant and a new production line. In Romania, Gedeon Richter has also launched a dedicated investment project to strengthen its manufacturing capacity. The company warns, however, that expanding pharmaceutical production takes time because of quality controls.The company also acknowledges that the measures adopted will not resolve the situation overnight. It says it is working so that the changes can improve supply as quickly as possible.A problem affecting other marketsThe shortage of Lenzetto is not limited to Spain. Gedeon Richter confirms that there is currently a global shortage of the medicine, although the severity of the problems varies between markets depending on local demand, forecasting capacity and logistical possibilities.The situation has for months made it difficult to obtain some hormone treatments used to relieve menopausal symptoms. The lack of Lenzetto forced patients and healthcare professionals to turn to other forms of estradiol, which eventually generated a domino effect on some of the alternative treatments.The European Medicines Agency (EMA) has also identified the Lenzetto shortage and is studying possible coordinated measures at the European level. In Spain, the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS) has likewise recorded supply problems affecting other medicines, such as Evopad, Estradot and Bijuva."The supply problem started in April with Lenzetto and has subsequently affected other transdermal hormone therapies such as patches and gels," AEMPS said in a statement (source in Spanish) published in early October. "The Ministry of Health has been in contact with the holders of other hormone treatment alternatives that are currently not reimbursed, to explore their possible inclusion in the pharmaceutical services of the National Health System."Richter responds to AEMPS criticismAEMPS has pointed out that some of the supply forecasts previously communicated by Gedeon Richter "have not always been accurate" and that interruptions which could affect the continuous supply of the medicine were not reported with sufficient notice.Asked by Euronews about these comments, the company does not directly address the allegations, but says it maintains "close contact" with AEMPS and works "in a collaborative manner" with the agency to tackle the situation.Gedeon Richter adds that it has improved its forecasting systems in response to demand it describes as "unprecedented" and that it continues to provide information to the authorities as new data become available.The laboratory does not, however, guarantee a full recovery of supply in the short term. The company says its goal is to be able to consistently meet patient demand from the second half of 2027.
